answer.line: Forward 4/6 and 5/6, back 3/6: 4/6 + 5/6 - 3/6 = 6/6, which is 1 mile.

steps: Picture the route as a line out from the start. Forward legs move you out; doubling back moves you in.
Put every leg in sixths: 2/3 = 4/6, 5/6 stays, 1/2 = 3/6.
Sense check: 1.5 miles out, half a mile back, 1 mile from the start.

choices.note: Renaming 1/2 as 2/6 takes back too little: 9/6 - 2/6 = 7/6. Half of six sixths is 3/6.
2 is every mile the driver covered, 4/6 + 5/6 + 3/6. True, but the stem asks how far from the start, so the half mile back comes off.
Renaming 1/2 as 4/6 takes back too much: 9/6 - 4/6 = 5/6. Half a mile is 3/6, not 4/6.
Reading doubles back 1/2 as halve the distance gives 3/2 x 1/2 = 3/4. Doubling back is a half-mile trip, so subtract it.

lockIt: Distance from the start is net: legs out add, legs back subtract. Rename to one denominator first.

playWith.label: Fractions, add and subtract: press Show why to see 1/2 split into quarters before adding

visual.alt: A number line in sixths from the start to 2 miles. Arcs go forward 4/6 and then 5/6 to 3/2, and a third arc comes back 3/6 to land on 1, outlined as the answer. A dashed marker at 2 shows the total miles driven.
visual.caption: Follow the arcs, not the odometer. Out to 3/2 and back to 1: the last arc decides where the driver stands.
